data.cultural_impact: Although the name Iraansh doesn't have a direct cultural reference to a historical or well-known figure in Hindu mythology, the name's roots are deeply grounded in the cultural beliefs and practices of the Hindu religion. The name signifies devotion and faith towards Lord Vishnu, who is an integral part of Hindu philosophy and cosmology. This name would resonate well with those who value spirituality and Hindu traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Iraansh has great spiritual significance in Hindu culture. The name Ira signifies the Lord Vishnu, who is considered the preserver of the universe and the sustainer of all living beings. The name Ansh signifies the divine presence or grace of the Lord. Together, the name implies that the one bearing the name is blessed and protected by the divine grace of Lord Vishnu. This name would serve as a constant reminder of the divine presence and the blessings of Lord Vishnu, providing a sense of spiritual security and peace.

historical_references.reference: Iranian dynasty of the Achaemenids, founded by Cyrus II the Great in 550 BCE, named their capital city Persepolis, also known as Persaea, which was a major center for Zoroastrianism. The name 'Iraansh' may be derived from the Achaemenid empire.

The Indian epic Mahabharata, written between 400 BCE and 200 CE, mentions the name 'Iran' and 'Iranians' in lineage of the Kuru dynasty. This could suggest that the name 'Iraansh' may have been used in ancient India as a reference to Persian heritage.
